title: Change Management
description: Lead the people side of change with Prosci ADKAR, Kotter's 8 steps, sponsorship, resistance management, and reinforcement.

questions.prompt: A clinic is moving to e-prescribing. In a pulse survey, pharmacists say they understand the regulatory reason for the change, but many add, "It adds steps for me and I see no benefit." Using Prosci ADKAR, where is the gap and what should the change team focus on?

options.text: Awareness: repeat the regulatory reasons for the change in a town hall
Knowledge: schedule more training sessions on the new software
Desire: address personal concerns and what is in it for them
Ability: give pharmacists hands-on practice time on the system

questions.explanation: The pharmacists already understand why (Awareness) but do not want to participate, which is a Desire gap; it is addressed through personal impact conversations, usually led by their managers. Repeating the business case targets an element they have already reached.

questions.prompt: A change manager is drafting a communication plan for a reorganization. One message explains why the company is restructuring; another explains how each employee's daily work will change. According to Prosci research on preferred senders, who should deliver the second message?

options.text: Each employee's direct supervisor
The CEO, in a company-wide town hall
The project manager running the reorganization
The HR or internal communications team

questions.explanation: Prosci research finds employees want to hear business reasons from senior leaders but personal impact ("what does this mean for me?") from their immediate supervisor. The CEO is the preferred sender for the first message, not the second.

questions.prompt: Two departments are being merged. Employees are visibly upset about losing their old team names, managers, and routines. Using William Bridges' Transition Model, what should leaders do first?

options.text: Launch the new combined team identity right away to move people past the old one
Present the financial business case again so people see the merger is logical
Wait quietly, because the neutral zone resolves itself once people adjust
Openly acknowledge what people are losing and mark the ending of the old way

questions.explanation: Bridges holds that every transition begins with an ending, so leaders must name and respect losses before people can move through the neutral zone to a new beginning. Rushing to a new identity skips the ending phase and tends to deepen resistance.

questions.prompt: True or false: Prosci research shows that the most commonly cited reason employees resist change is fear of losing their jobs.
questions.explanation: Prosci's research consistently finds the top reason is lack of awareness of why the change is being made, which is why sponsors communicating the business reasons matters so much. Fear of job loss appears on the list but is not the most common cause.

questions.prompt: Put these six of Kotter's 8 steps for leading change in the order Kotter prescribes.

lines.text: Anchor new approaches in the culture

questions.explanation: Kotter's sequence is urgency, guiding coalition, vision and strategy, communicate the vision, empower broad-based action, short-term wins, consolidate gains, and anchor in the culture. Culture change comes last because new behaviors must first prove they produce results.

questions.prompt: A change manager runs a Prosci ADKAR assessment for the billing team (1 = low, 5 = high). Where should she focus effort next?

code.source:
Billing team - average ADKAR scores
Awareness      4
Desire         4
Knowledge      2
Ability        2
Reinforcement  3

options.text: Reinforcement, so the gains already made are not lost
Knowledge, because it is the first element scoring 3 or lower
Ability, because job performance is what the business measures
Desire, because every element after it scores lower than it

questions.explanation: Prosci defines the barrier point as the first ADKAR element scoring 3 or lower; elements build in sequence, so Ability cannot improve until people know how to change. Ability ties for the lowest score, but working on it before Knowledge is addressed wastes effort.

questions.prompt: The VP sponsoring an ERP rollout approved the budget, then told the change manager, "You handle the people stuff," and has not appeared at any employee event since. Based on Prosci research, what should the change manager push for?

options.text: Nothing; the change manager owns adoption, so the sponsor's job ends once funding is secured
Ask the sponsor to fund extra change staff so the team can cover the communications instead
Ask the sponsor to send one company-wide email endorsing the project, then step back again
Coach the sponsor to be active and visible, build a sponsor coalition, and explain the why directly

questions.explanation: Prosci's research names active and visible sponsorship as the top contributor to change success; sponsors must participate throughout, build a coalition of peer sponsors, and communicate the reasons directly. Funding more change staff cannot substitute for the authority only the sponsor has.

questions.prompt: Prosci separates the technical (project) side of a change from the people side. For a new expense system, which of these activities are people-side change management work? Select all that apply.

options.text: Assessing how much each employee group's daily work will change
Building the cutover schedule and data migration plan
Coaching supervisors to recognize and manage resistance
Configuring approval workflows in the expense software
Designing recognition and reinforcement for new behaviors
Writing and running the system test plan

questions.explanation: Impact assessment by group, supervisor coaching for resistance, and reinforcement all help individuals adopt the change, which is the people side. Cutover planning, configuration, and testing deliver the technical solution and belong to project management.

questions.prompt: A senior analyst, normally a top performer, is openly criticizing the new workflow tool in team meetings. Following Prosci's resistance-management guidance, what should her team lead do first?

options.text: Meet one-on-one to listen and find the root cause, such as which ADKAR element is missing
Escalate to HR as a conduct issue so that others see resistance has consequences
Leave her out of change meetings for now so her criticism does not spread to the team
Ask the sponsor for a company-wide message stating that use of the tool is mandatory

questions.explanation: Prosci treats resistance as a normal reaction and says to identify its root cause before acting, with the supervisor as the primary resistance manager; ADKAR is the diagnostic. Escalating or excluding her treats the symptom and often entrenches the resistance.

questions.prompt: Six weeks after a CRM go-live, the project manager wants to close the project. What do these adoption metrics show?

code.source:
Week 6 after CRM go-live
Licensed users who logged in this week:        96%
New opportunities created in the CRM:          41%
Deals still tracked in personal spreadsheets:  58%
CRM records with required fields complete:     47%

options.text: Adoption is successful because nearly all users log in, so the project can close
The only problem is data quality, which mandatory-field validation rules will fix
Logins are high but utilization and proficiency are low, so benefits are not yet realized
The software is defective, since most users cannot create opportunities in it

questions.explanation: Prosci ties project benefits to speed of adoption, ultimate utilization, and proficiency; most work still happens in spreadsheets and records are incomplete, so the change has not been adopted despite logins. Login counts measure access, not the new way of working.

questions.prompt: Seven months into an 18-month transformation, there are no visible results yet, and skeptics are telling colleagues the initiative is failing. Following Kotter's model, what should the guiding coalition do now?

options.text: Restart at step 1 with a new burning platform to rebuild a sense of urgency
Plan and deliver visible, unambiguous wins soon and recognize the people behind them
Rewrite the vision statement so it better answers the skeptics' objections
Hold off reporting any results until the full transformation is complete

questions.explanation: Kotter's short-term wins step exists to show progress within months, undercut cynics, and keep momentum through a long change. Withholding results until the end is exactly what lets skeptics define the story.

questions.prompt: Nine months into a lean transformation, the pilot plant hits all its targets. The CEO announces "mission accomplished," disbands the guiding coalition, and moves the change budget elsewhere. A year later the plant's metrics have slid back to baseline. Which of Kotter's change errors does this illustrate?

options.text: Declaring victory too soon, before the changes were consolidated and anchored in the culture
Failing to establish a great enough sense of urgency at the start of the transformation
Under-communicating the vision, so employees never understood where the change was heading
Not creating a powerful enough guiding coalition to drive the transformation forward

questions.explanation: Kotter warns that celebrating a win is fine, but declaring the war won removes momentum before new practices are rooted in norms, systems, and promotions, so old behavior returns. The coalition was powerful enough to hit the targets; the error was dissolving it too early.

questions.prompt: Each project below rated its own impact on the call center as acceptable. Since July, call center productivity has fallen 12% and absenteeism has doubled. What should the change lead do?

code.source:
Changes landing on the call center, Q3
Project               | Impact on agents | Go-live
New CRM               | High             | Jul 8
New shift schedule    | High             | Jul 15
QA scorecard redesign | Medium           | Aug 1
Office relocation     | Medium           | Aug 19

options.text: Have each project double its own communications so agents better understand every change
Add more CRM training, since the CRM is the highest-impact change on the list
Proceed as planned, since every project assessed its own impact on agents as acceptable
Assess cumulative impact on agents across projects and work with leaders to resequence

questions.explanation: This is change saturation: impacts that are acceptable one project at a time overwhelm a group when they land together, so impact must be assessed per group across the portfolio and changes sequenced or paused. More communication from every project adds to the overload rather than relieving it.

questions.prompt: A company gave its supervisors a toolkit for coaching their teams through a new performance-review process. A pulse survey shows 40% of the supervisors themselves do not support the change, and their teams' adoption is lagging. What should the change team do?

options.text: Bypass the supervisors and have the change team brief their frontline staff directly
Reissue the coaching toolkit with more detailed scripts and talking points
Take supervisors through their own ADKAR transition first, then equip them to coach
Make the coaching sessions mandatory and track completion in supervisors' goals

questions.explanation: Prosci notes managers are both employees experiencing the change and coaches for others; they must be engaged as individuals (Awareness, Desire, and so on) before they can credibly lead their teams. Bypassing them removes the preferred sender for personal-impact messages, and better scripts do not fix a supervisor's own Desire gap.

questions.prompt: Sales reps completed CRM training and pass proficiency checks, yet most still log deals in personal spreadsheets. What is the root cause, and what fixes it?

code.source:
Sales compensation:   paid on closed revenue only
Weekly pipeline call: managers review reps' own spreadsheets
CRM logging policy:   "required", but never checked or discussed

options.text: A Knowledge gap; run refresher training focused on entering opportunities in the CRM
Reinforcement rewards the old way; managers must run reviews from CRM data and measure its use
An Awareness gap; have the sponsor resend the business case for adopting the new CRM
A tool-fit problem; reps prefer spreadsheets, so the company should change CRM vendors

questions.explanation: The reps have the Knowledge and Ability, but every organizational signal (pipeline reviews, measures, unenforced policy) still reinforces spreadsheets, so Reinforcement and manager behavior must change. More training addresses an element the proficiency checks show is already in place.
